ielts.totalNote: Academic version; Listening includes 10-minute transfer time

sections.name: Listening
sections.tests: Understanding conversations, lectures, and monologues in English; native and non-native accents

sections.name: Reading
sections.tests: Comprehension of academic texts: essays, journal extracts, research articles; matching, multiple choice, short answers

sections.name: Writing
sections.tests: Task 1: describe a graph, chart, diagram, or process (150 words, 20 min); Task 2: formal essay on statement/question (250 words, 40 min)

sections.name: Speaking
sections.tests: Part 1: one-on-one interview on familiar topics (4–5 min); Part 2: 2-minute speech on topic card (3–4 min); Part 3: discussion with examiner (4–5 min)

benchmarks: Band 6.0–6.5: accepted by most universities; entry-level for UK/Australia visas
Band 7.0–7.5: competitive for top 50 universities; preferred by professional bodies (nursing, engineering)
Band 8.0+: advanced fluency; required for graduate research, leadership roles
tips: Listening: familiarize yourself with all three accents (British, American, Australian) used in IELTS tests—train on podcasts and documentaries
Reading: strict time management—allocate 18–20 minutes per passage to avoid rushing; skim headings and topic sentences first
Speaking: prioritize fluency and coherence over perfect grammar; examiners reward natural speech patterns and relevant examples

toefl.totalNote: iBT format (shortened July 2023); no breaks between sections; integrated tasks test multiple skills per task

sections.name: Reading
sections.tests: Academic texts (620–680 words); comprehension, vocabulary, inference, main idea; multiple choice, select-all-that-apply, drag-and-drop

sections.name: Listening
sections.tests: Academic conversations (2–3 min) and lectures (3–5 min); understanding main idea, details, inference, speaker attitude; multiple choice, select-all-that-apply

sections.name: Speaking
sections.tests: Task 1: independent (15 sec prep, 45 sec response); Tasks 2–4: integrated (read/listen, then speak 30–60 sec)

sections.name: Writing
sections.tests: Task 1: integrated (read 3 min + listen 2 min, write 20 min, 150–225 words); Task 2: writing for an academic discussion (30 min, 100+ words)

benchmarks: Score 80–90: accepted by most US universities; entry-level for graduate programs
Score 100–110: competitive for top 50 universities; preferred by strong master's programs
Score 110+: excellent for PhD, research positions, postdoctoral roles
tips: Reading: use skimming and scanning techniques—read topic sentences and the first question before diving into full text
Listening: take organized notes (abbreviations, key terms) during lectures—you can reference them during questions
Writing: in integrated tasks, synthesize information from reading and listening; in academic discussion, respond conversationally to peers while maintaining academic tone

pte.totalNote: Delivered on computer; speaking and writing are recorded; no writing on paper

sections.name: Speaking & Writing
sections.tests: Personal introduction, read aloud (40–60 sec), repeat sentence, describe image, re-tell lecture (3 min), answer short question, summarize written text, write essay (200–300 words)

sections.name: Reading
sections.tests: Multiple choice (single + multiple answers), re-order paragraphs (jumbled text), fill in blanks (drag-and-drop vocabulary)

sections.name: Listening
sections.tests: Summarize spoken text (30–40 sec recording, write 50–70 word summary), fill blanks (listening comprehension), multiple choice, highlight correct summary, write from dictation

benchmarks: Score 50–58: accepted by most Australian universities and some UK institutions
Score 65+: competitive for top universities; visa requirement for Australia/UK skilled migration
Score 79+: excellent; required for professional registration (nursing, engineering, accounting)
tips: Speaking: enunciate clearly and maintain steady pace—machine-scored, so clear pronunciation is critical; background noise is automatically detected and may lower score
Reading: practice re-ordering paragraphs using logical flow and transition words as clues—this section trips many test-takers
Listening: the writing-from-dictation task rewards careful listening—use headphones, listen actively, and replay if available

celpip.totalNote: Canadian English pronunciation; General version (not Academic); human-scored speaking
celpip.scoring: CLB 4–12 (Canadian Language Benchmarks, converted to 0–10 in reports)

sections.name: Listening
sections.tests: Conversations and monologues; multiple choice, multiple answers, short answer, matching; Canadian English accents and contexts

sections.name: Reading
sections.tests: Emails, notices, instructions, passages; multiple choice, multiple answers, short answer, matching, cloze (fill in blanks)

sections.name: Writing
sections.tests: Task 1: email or letter (150–200 words, 20 min); Task 2: essay or response (150–250 words, 36 min)

sections.name: Speaking
sections.tests: Greetings, read-aloud (20 sec), describe photo, describe graph, sustain a conversation, spontaneous speech, persuade, summarize (30–45 sec each)

benchmarks: CLB 7–8 (CELPIP 8–9): entry-level for Canadian skilled immigration; most universities accept this
CLB 9 (CELPIP 10): competitive for professional roles and graduate programs
CLB 10–12 (CELPIP 11–12): advanced fluency; required for healthcare and regulated professions
tips: Speaking: CELPIP is scored by humans, not machines—engage naturally with the prompts, smile in your tone, and provide relevant examples
Listening: Canadian English vocabulary and idioms differ from US English—familiarize yourself with Canadian media, podcasts, and news
Writing: emphasis is on clarity and relevance—organize your ideas with clear topic sentences and avoid overly complex structures

duolingo.totalNote: Online, proctored; mobile-first design; adaptive difficulty; results in 2 days

sections.name: Listening & Speaking
sections.tests: Listening comprehension, reading comprehension, repeating sentences, speaking spontaneously to prompts; adaptive—harder questions appear after correct answers

sections.name: Reading & Writing
sections.tests: Multiple choice, fill in blanks, translation (into/from English), writing short responses; adaptive difficulty

benchmarks: Score 100–110: entry-level for most universities; some top schools require 120+
Score 120–130: competitive for selective universities and graduate programs
Score 130+: excellent; equivalent to TOEFL 100+ or IELTS 7.0+
tips: Preparation: Duolingo English Test adapts to your level—correct answers trigger harder questions, so don't aim for perfection on easy questions
Speaking: speak naturally and at a conversational pace—the system evaluates fluency, not accent, so clarity matters more than perfection
Environment: test in a quiet room with stable internet; camera and microphone must work clearly; any suspicious behavior may trigger retakes

gre.totalNote: General Test (shortened September 2023); adaptive by section; 1-minute break between Verbal and Quant
gre.scoring: 130–170 per section (Verbal, Quant); 0–6 for Analytical Writing

sections.name: Analytical Writing
sections.tests: Analyze an Issue: write an essay (500–600 words) taking a position on a given statement; identify implications, support reasoning, counterarguments

sections.name: Verbal Reasoning
sections.tests: Reading comprehension (8 Q), text completion (8 Q), sentence equivalence (11 Q); vocabulary, logic, inference

sections.name: Quantitative Reasoning
sections.tests: Algebra, arithmetic, data analysis, probability, word problems; quantitative comparison, multiple choice, numeric entry; focus on applications and reasoning over computation

benchmarks: Score 150–160 (Verbal + Quant): entry-level for master's programs in STEM/business
Score 160–165: competitive for top 20 universities across most fields
Score 165+: excellent for PhD programs, research-intensive master's, top consulting/finance roles
tips: Verbal: sentence equivalence tests synonym recognition—both correct answers must be semantically identical, not just similar
Quant: the 2023 shortened test focuses on data analysis and reasoning—practice graphs, charts, and probability over complex geometry calculations
Adaptive testing: your second section difficulty depends on your first section score—aim for consistency across both verbal and quant

gmat.totalNote: GMAT Focus Edition (launched 2023); three 45-minute sections + optional 10-minute break; no Analytical Writing essay
gmat.scoring: 205–805 (composite); 60–90 each for Verbal, Quantitative, Data Insights

sections.name: Verbal
sections.tests: Critical Reasoning (13 Q): evaluate arguments, identify assumptions, strengthen/weaken arguments; Reading Comprehension (10 Q): passage analysis, inference, main idea

sections.name: Quantitative
sections.tests: Problem Solving only — algebra, arithmetic, word problems and number properties. Data Sufficiency moved to Data Insights and geometry was removed in the Focus Edition.

sections.name: Data Insights
sections.tests: Data Sufficiency, Multi-Source Reasoning, Table Analysis, Graphics Interpretation and Two-Part Analysis — interpret and combine data across formats.

benchmarks: Score 645–700: entry-level for top MBA programs (including Ivy League); equivalent to old GMAT ~700
Score 700–750: competitive for select MBA programs (top 10–20); some scholarships available
Score 750+: excellent; highly competitive for MBA, EMBA, and funded fellowship roles
tips: Verbal: Critical Reasoning remains central—practice identifying logical fallacies and argument structure; Reading passages are shorter (3–4 min) but business-focused
Quantitative: focus on Problem Solving—brush up on geometry (circles, triangles, 3D shapes) and probability; no data sufficiency means reasoning over pure calculation
Data Insights: the newest section tests real-world thinking—practice interpreting Excel-like tables, pivot tables, and statistical trends; this section is less computational and more interpretive
